tu-vs-vous.title: "Tu" or "vous"?
tu-vs-vous.body: Tu is informal — used with friends, family and people your own age. Vous is formal (used with strangers, superiors, older people) and is also the plural "you". When in doubt, always start with vous — it's safer than sounding too familiar.

tu-es-contraction.title: "Tu es" becomes "t'es" in speech
tu-es-contraction.body: It would be "Tu es français ?", but in fast speech almost nobody pronounces the two words separately — tu es becomes t'es. It's so common that it even shows up in informal written messages: "T'es français ?". In the exercises here, keep writing the standard form tu es — the contraction is just for recognizing it when you hear or read it.

comment-tappelles-wh-in-situ.title: "Comment tu t'appelles ?" also becomes "Tu t'appelles comment ?"
comment-tappelles-wh-in-situ.body: In everyday speech it's just as common, or even more so, to leave the question word ("comment") at the END of the sentence, keeping the normal subject-verb order — tu t'appelles comment ? instead of "comment tu t'appelles ?". In the exercises here, keep using the order with "comment" at the start — it's the form both exercises here ask for.

trueFalse.claim: This question is used to find out someone's age.
trueFalse.whyNote: Wrong — comment tu t'appelles ? asks for the NAME (appeler = to be called), not the age. For age you'd say "quel âge as-tu ?".
